newsitem.title: CROATIA: Six Croat policemen charged over Mostar attack.
newsitem.headline: Six Croat policemen charged over Mostar attack.

text.p: Bosnian Croats in the divided city of Mostar will prosecute six policemen suspected of involvement in an attack on a group of Moslems this month, Croatia's state news agency HINA reported on Thursday.

"The investigation into the role and activities of the police officers found they had breached their authority and used force inappropriate to the situation," said an official statement quoted by HINA.

Obe person was killed and 22 were injured on February 10 when Moslems were attacked while trying to visit a cemetery in Croat-held western Mostar. It was the most violent incident since the Bosnian war stopped in December 1995.
According to witnesses and photographs possessed by NATO, uniformed Croat police stood by as men armed with guns and clubs assaulted the procession of 200 Moslems.
The six policemen, who were not identified, were removed from duty pending the final results of the investigation, HINA said.
